change: Extend the bounded source observer with an immutable byte-snapshot normalizer. It reserves all syntactically valid known 32-bit handle candidates, assigns distinct non-sentinel aliases to the selected wide identities, refuses unselected wide handle candidates, adjusts the qualified HANDSEED, and replaces only validated physical value spans. It re-observes the result and retains the original source lexemes and identity mapping. It does not modify existing import, consumer or writer routes.

validation.focused: PASS compact graph CTest and GCC warning-clean syntax check. Generated ASCII/Binary cases cover wide input, collisions with handles 1 and 2, alternate dictionary role, literal text containing a handle spelling, unexpected external wide references, incorrect or missing HANDSEED, malformed reference, 17-digit overflow, narrow-only refusal, oversized input, cleared failure state, a source view aliasing prior output, and corrected retry. CRLF ASCII succeeds.
validation.peer: For the full locally authored ezdxf 1.4.5 graph, the component prepared ASCII and Binary inputs with alias mapping 100000010->2F and 100000011->30, HANDSEED->34. Independent tag comparison found exactly seven expected handle-value changes; all other tags were unchanged. The existing converter then accepted both prepared files. Independent ezdxf readback compared the original wide source against output: 25 mapped objects, 24 dictionary entries, 13 root entries, two layers, ownership, reactors, XRECORD reference, MATERIAL body and DICTIONARYVAR values; zero audit errors/fixes.

limits: This is a separate preparatory component; the public reader still refuses the wide source and the writer has not bound the original graph to its output. No end-to-end wide support or producer-independent semantics is claimed.
A trial using an external semantic serializer changed unrelated metadata, so the implemented component uses validated physical spans instead.
No DXF/DWG fixture is committed; all source and output drawings are scratch-only.
